_schemaNote: toneCurve points are [x, y] pairs, e.g. [0.25, 0.24] -- NOT {"x":...,"y":...} objects. See golden_hour.json's _schemaNote for the device bug this avoids.
_tuningNote: TUNED from hand-graded Lightroom reference values. Conversions, matching golden_hour.json's own methodology: EV->brightness via a mid-gray anchor (0.5*(2^EV-1)); LR Saturation/Vibrance percent -> CIColorControls.saturation / CIVibrance.amount at 1:1 (1.0+LR/100, LR/100); temperature as a mired-space delta against the fixed 6500K/tint-0 baseline (positive LR Temperature = warm = LOWER resulting Kelvin, confirmed empirically, same direction as Golden Hour); tint at 4x LR's raw number (Golden Hour's empirically-found multiplier) with NEGATIVE targetNeutral.y = magenta / POSITIVE = green (re-confirmed empirically this session, see _tuningNoteContrast for Y2K's cool-direction and Deep Teal-equivalent-in-travel_film's green-direction checks); vignette radius and grain size are NOT given by the reference (only intensity numbers) -- chosen to match Golden Hour's own established range (radius 1.2-1.6) and each variant's aesthetic (grain size finer for Y2K's digital-sensor look, coarser for film-like Polaroid/Light Leak), flagged as interpretation. 'Faded blacks' was checked against each variant's own tone-curve black point (point0) and found numerically identical in all three variants (same data given twice) -- fade is dropped from every chain, as in Golden Hour. Bloom radius-as-percent-of-width converted to pixels against the 1280px preview reference width, matching Golden Hour.
_tuningNoteContrast: colorControls.contrast and .brightness are 1.0/0.0 (neutral, no-op) for EVERY variant in this pack, NOT a converted LR value. This is a deliberate, empirically-verified choice: a fresh CIColorControls.contrast sweep this session (both directions, not just reductions like Golden Hour's own round-3 check) confirmed contrast is non-linear enough that even a SMALL deviation from 1.0 shifts the tone curve's effective black/white points once colorControls runs before toneCurve (the established correct op order) -- e.g. a damped ~1:10 LR-contrast conversion (the gentlest scale tried) still measurably shifted a variant's near-black output away from its tone curve's own intended point0. Rather than re-deriving a separate damping constant per variant, this pack follows Golden Hour Soft Glow's own resolution directly: colorControls' contrast/brightness are neutralized and EVERY variant's 5-point tone curve (built straight from that variant's own reference tone-curve values, which already encode its real contrast/exposure character) carries 100% of the tonal shaping. Y2K Digicam's cool direction (temperature 8275K, tint -20, against the 6500K/tint-0 baseline) was verified with a throwaway CoreImage script on both a neutral gray and a warm photo-like base color -- the blue channel measurably exceeds red in both cases, confirming it renders cooler, not warmer, despite the counter-intuitive mired-space sign (matching Golden Hour's own established, re-verified-here direction).
